title: Definition
body_md:
The operator $\mathcal{P}:\mathscr{H}\to 2^{\mathscr{H}}$ is called 
\emph{$\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone} if $\exists$ a constant 
$\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}\in\mathbb{R}$ s. t.
\[
\langle w-y,\,u-v\rangle
\ge
\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}\|w-y\|^2,
\quad
\forall w,y\in \mathscr{H},\ 
u\in \mathcal{P}(w),\ 
v\in \mathcal{P}(y).
\]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
\cite{Minh}
A $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone operator $\mathcal{P}$ is maximal if no proper $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone extension of $\mathcal{P}$ exists.\\
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The parameter $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$ may be negative. 
The case $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}=0$ corresponds to classical monotonicity, 
$\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0$ corresponds to strong monotonicity, 
and $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}<0$ describes weak monotonicity.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
We say that $\mathcal{Q}:\mathscr{H}\to\mathscr{H}$ is
\begin{itemize}
    \item Lipschitz continuous with $ \xi\ge 0$ if
    \[
    \|\mathcal{Q}(w_1)-\mathcal{Q}(w_2)\|\le  \xi\|w_1-w_2\|,
    \qquad \forall w_1,w_2\in\mathscr{H};
    \]
    \item \emph{$\zeta$-cocoercive} if
    \[
    \langle \mathcal{Q}(w_1)-\mathcal{Q}(w_2),\,w_1-w_2\rangle
    \ge
    \zeta\|\mathcal{Q}(w_1)-\mathcal{Q}(w_2)\|^2,
    \qquad \forall w_1,w_2\in\mathscr{H}.
    \]
\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: GENMON
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{GENMON}\cite{Minh}
Let $\mathcal{P}:\mathscr{H}\to 2^{\mathscr{H}}$ be a $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone set-valued operator and $\mathcal{Q}:\mathscr{H}\to\mathscr{H}$ be a single-valued mapping. 
Assume that $\mu>0$ satisfies $1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0$. Consequently, we have:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item  $\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}$ is single-valued.
    \item $\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}$ is $(1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}})$-cocoercive.
    \item $\mathrm{dom}\,\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}=\mathscr{H}$ $\iff$ $\mathcal{P}$ is maximal $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone.\\
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem fixed point
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem fixed point}\cite{NHVF} Suppose the operator $\mathcal{P}:\mathscr{H}\to 2^{\mathscr{H}}$ is $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone and $\mathcal{Q}:\mathscr{H}\to\mathscr{H}$ be single-valued. 
If $\mu>0$ satisfies $1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0$, then a point ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\in\mathscr{H}$ solves the IP \eqref{inc1} $\iff$
\[
\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}({\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*-\mu\mathcal{Q}({\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*))={\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,
\]
that is,
\[
{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\in \mathrm{Fix}\!\left(\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}(\mathcal{I}-\mu\mathcal{Q})\right).
\]
head: environment

label: ICAsmmain
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ICAsmmain}
The operator $\mathcal{P}$ is maximal $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone, and $\mathcal{Q}$ is $\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}$-monotone as well as $\xi$-Lipschitz continuous. 
Moreover, $\mu>0$ is chosen s. t.
\[
1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0,
\quad ; \quad
2(\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}})+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}^{2}-\mu  \xi^{2}>0.
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It follows from \cite{NHVF} that Assumption~\eqref{ICAsmmain} is valid under any of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}>0$.
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}=0 \ ; \ \Pi_{\mathcal{P}}^{2}> \xi^{2}$.
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}<0$ \ ; \ $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}> \xi$.\\
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: tr1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\cite{NHVF,PDINC}\label{tr1}
Let $\mathcal{P}:\mathscr{H}\to2^{\mathscr{H}}$ be a $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone set-valued operator and $\mathcal{Q}:\mathscr{H}\to\mathscr{H}$ be a single-valued mapping. Suppose that Assumption~\eqref{ICAsmmain} holds and define
\[
\Psi(w):=\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}(w-\mu\mathcal{Q}(w)),
\qquad \mu>0.
\]
Then, $\exists \ \aleph\in(0,1)$, the following holds for every
\(w\in\mathscr{H}\setminus\{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}^{*}\}\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \label{patr1} The operator $\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}}\circ (\mathcal{I}-\mu \mathcal{Q})$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $\aleph$.
    
    \item \label{pbtr1} The fixed-point set $\mathrm{Fix}\!\left(\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}}\circ (\mathcal{I}-\mu \mathcal{Q})\right)$ is nonempty and singleton.
    
    \item \label{pctr1} $\|\Psi(w)- {\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|\leq \aleph\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|, \ \forall \ {\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\in \mbox{\rm Fix}(\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}} (\mathcal{I}-\mu \mathcal{Q}))$.
    
    \item \label{pdtr1} $(1- \aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2\leq \langle w-\Psi(w) ,w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^* \rangle$.
    
    \item \label{petr1} $(1- \aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|\leq \|w-\Psi(w)\|\leq (1+\aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|$.
    
    \item \label{pftr1} $\langle w-\Psi(w) ,w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^* \rangle \leq (1+\aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2$.\\ 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: rem2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{rem2}
Suppose $\mathcal{P}:\mathscr{H}\to2^{\mathscr{H}}$ be a $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone set-valued operator and 
$\mathcal{Q}:\mathscr{H}\to\mathscr{H}$ be a single-valued mapping. 
Assume that $\mu>0$ satisfies $1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0$ and that Assumption~\eqref{ICAsmmain} hold. 
Then IP \eqref{inc1} admits a unique solution.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From Part~\eqref{pbtr1} of Lemma~\ref{tr1}, the operator 
$\mathscr{R}_{\mu\mathcal{P}}\circ(\mathcal{I}-\mu\mathcal{Q})$
possesses a unique fixed point. 
By Lemma~\ref{lem fixed point}, this fixed point is equivalent to the unique solution of the IP~\eqref{inc1}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Observe that Assumption~\eqref{ICAsmmain} is satisfied whenever the parameters 
$\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}, \Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}, L$, and $\mu$ fulfill one of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}>0$.
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}=0$ and $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}^{2}> \xi^{2}$.
    \item $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}+\Pi_{\mathcal{Q}}<0$ and $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}> \xi$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, under any of these conditions, the solution of the problem \eqref{inc1} exists and is uniquely determined.

label: lem2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\cite{TVl1}\label{lem2}
Suppose that $\exists$ a continuously differentiable function
$\mathcal{L}:[s_0,+\infty)\times\mathscr{H} \to \mathbb{R}_+$, which positive definite
satisfying
\begin{equation}
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s)) \le
-m_1 \phi_1(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\vartheta_1}(s,w(s))
-m_2 \phi_2(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\vartheta_2}(s,w(s)),
\label{eq_lemma_condition}
\end{equation}
where $m_1>0$, $m_2>0$, $0<\vartheta_1<1$, $\vartheta_2>1$ and 
\(
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w) :=
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial s}(s,w)
+
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial w}(s,w)\dot w.
\)
Suppose $\phi_1,\phi_2:[s_0,+\infty)\to \mathbb{R}_{++}$ be continuous.
Define
\[
\mathcal{F}_1(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \phi_1(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\qquad
\mathcal{F}_2(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \phi_2(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa}.
\]
If
\(
\frac{1}{m_2(\vartheta_2-1)}
<
\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \phi_2(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa}
\)
and
\(
\mathcal{F}_1\!\circ\!\mathcal{F}_2^{-1}
\!\left(
\frac{1}{m_2(\vartheta_2-1)}
\right)
+
\frac{1}{m_1(1-\vartheta_1)}
<
\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \phi_1(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\)
then $\exists$ $\mathcal{T}>s_0$ such that $\mathcal{L}(s,w(s))\equiv0, \ \forall \ s\ge \mathcal{T}$.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{T} \le
\mathcal{F}_1^{-1}
\left(
\mathcal{F}_1\!\circ\!\mathcal{F}_2^{-1}
\!\left(
\frac{1}{m_2(\vartheta_2-1)}
\right)
+
\frac{1}{m_1(1-\vartheta_1)}
\right).
\label{eq_T_bound_lemma}
\end{equation}

label: prop3.1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop3.1}
Suppose $\mathcal{P} : \mathscr{H} \to 2^{\mathscr{H}}$ be $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone and $\mathcal{Q} : \mathscr{H} \to \mathscr{H}$ be single-valued. If $\mu>0$ satisfies $1+\mu\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}>0$, then ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^* \in \mathscr{H}$ is a solution of \eqref{inc1} $\iff$ it is an equilibrium point of \eqref{1stNDS}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The assertion is a direct consequence of Lemma~\ref{lem fixed point}, where the solutions of \eqref{inc1} are characterized as the fixed points of $\Psi$, together with the definition of equilibrium of \eqref{1stNDS}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item As we take  $\phi_2(s) = 1$, TVCNDM \eqref{INFxTM} is become
\[
\dot{w} = -\phi_1(s) \Sigma(w) \left[ \|w-\Psi(w)\|^{\lambda_1} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{\phi_1(s)} \|w-\Psi(w)\|^{\lambda_2- \lambda_1} \right) \right].
\]

\item If $b_2=0$ and $\phi_1(s)$ is a constant function, then the model \eqref{INFxTM} reduces to the nominal model studied in \cite{NH}, namely
\begin{equation}\label{reduemodel}
\dot{w}(s)
=
-\sigma\big(w(s)-\Psi(w)\big),
\end{equation}
where $\sigma>0$. 
Then model \eqref{reduemodel} was analyzed in \cite{NH} in the context of finite-time stability for generalized monotone IPs.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop3.5
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop3.5}
The models \eqref{1stNDS} and \eqref{INFxTM} share the same equilibrium points.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The claim follows immediately from \eqref{dnrho}, by the definition of $\theta(\cdot,s)$.
Indeed,
\[
\theta(w,s)=0
\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
w \in \mathrm{Fix}\!\left(\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}} \circ (\mathcal{I}-\mu \mathcal{Q})\right),
\]
which matches the equilibrium condition of model \eqref{1stNDS}.
head: environment

label: prop3.6
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop3.6}
Suppose $\mathcal{P} : \mathscr{H} \to 2^{\mathscr{H}}$, $\mathcal{Q} : \mathscr{H} \to \mathscr{H}$, and $\mu>0$ satisfy Assumption~\eqref{ICAsmmain}. Then ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$ solves the IP \eqref{inc1} $\iff$ it is an equilibrium point of \eqref{INFxTM}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Combining Propositions~\ref{prop3.5} and~\ref{prop3.1} yields the desired conclusion.
head: environment

label: unique sol da sy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\cite{Zheng}\label{unique sol da sy}
Consider the model \eqref{INFxTM}. Suppose that the mapping $\Psi: \mathscr{H}\to \mathscr{H}$ is locally Lipschitz continuous and satisfies
\[
\Psi({\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*)={\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*
\quad\text{and}\quad
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\, w-\Psi(w)\rangle>0,
\quad
\forall w\in\mathscr{H}\setminus\{{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\},
\]
for some ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\in \mathscr{H}$. Then the vector field of \eqref{INFxTM} is continuous on $\mathscr{H}$, and for any initial condition the differential equation admits a unique global solution defined for all $s\ge0$.\\
head: environment

label: rem3
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem3}
Define
\(
\Psi(w):=\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}}\big(w-\mu \mathcal{Q}(w)\big),
\ w\in\mathscr{H}.
\)
By Lemma~\ref{tr1}, the operator $\Psi$ possesses a unique fixed point ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$, and hence the model admits a unique equilibrium. Moreover, for any $w\neq {\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq13}
\begin{aligned}
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*, w-\Psi(w)\rangle
&=
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2
+
\left\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\,
{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*-\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}}(w-\mu \mathcal{Q}(w))
\right\rangle .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Applying the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality together with Lemma~\ref{tr1} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq14}
\left\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\, 
{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*-\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}}(w-\mu \mathcal{Q}(w))
\right\rangle
\ge
-\,\aleph\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2,
\end{equation}
for some $\aleph\in(0,1)$. Combining \eqref{eq13} and \eqref{eq14}, we obtain
\[
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\, w-\Psi(w)\rangle
\ge
(1-\aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2
>
0,
\qquad
\forall w\in\mathscr{H}\setminus\{{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\}.
\]
head: environment

label: tr2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{tr2}
Consider an $\Pi_{\mathcal{P}}$-monotone set-valued mapping $\mathcal{P}: \mathscr{H} \to 2^\mathscr{H}$ and a single-valued operator $\mathcal{Q}: \mathscr{H} \to \mathscr{H} $, along with a positive parameter $\mu$ s. t.  assumption \eqref{ICAsmmain} is satisfied. Furthermore, Suppose that
\(
\frac{1}{m_2(\vartheta_2-1)}
<
\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \phi_2(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa}
\)
and
\(
{\mathcal{F}}_1\!\circ\!{\mathcal{F}}_2^{-1}
\left(
\frac{1}{m_2(\vartheta_2-1)}
\right)
+
\frac{1}{m_1(1-\vartheta_1)}
<
\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \phi_1(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\)
where
\(
\vartheta_1=\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2},\
\vartheta_2=\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2},
\
m_1=
2^{\vartheta_1}
\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}},
\) and \(
m_2=
2^{\vartheta_2}(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2}
\)  for some $
\aleph\in(0,1)$ with
\[
{\mathcal{F}}_1(s)=\int_0^s \phi_1(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\qquad
{\mathcal{F}}_2(s)=\int_0^s \phi_2(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\]
then $w(s)$ of \eqref{INFxTM} converges to ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$ with settling time in \eqref{eq_T_bound_lemma}.
head: environment

label: THL1
title: Proof
body_md:
The operator 
\(
\mathscr{R}_{\mu \mathcal{P}} \circ (\mathcal{I} - \mu \mathcal{Q})
\)  holds (i) condition of Lemma~\ref{tr1}, 
Moreover, by Theorem~\ref{rem2}, the IP admits a unique solution. In addition, Remark~\ref{rem3} ensures that the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{unique sol da sy} are satisfied. Consequently, the TVCNDM \eqref{INFxTM} admits a unique global solution for every initial condition and is well defined for all forward times.\\
\noindent
Consider the Lyapunov function candidate
\begin{equation}\label{THL1}
\mathcal{L}(s,w(s))=\frac{1}{2}\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2.
\end{equation}
Then $\mathcal{L}(w)=0 \iff w={\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$ and $\mathcal{L}(w)\to\infty$ as $\|w\|\to\infty$. Taking the time derivative of \eqref{THL1}, we obtain
\begin{align}
\notag\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
&=
\left\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\dot w\right\rangle
\\
&=
-
\left(
\phi_1(s)\frac{1}{\|w-\Psi(w)\|^{1-\lambda_1}}
+
\phi_2(s)\frac{1}{\|w-\Psi(w)\|^{1-\lambda_2}}
\right)
\cdot
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*, w-\Psi(w)\rangle.
\end{align}
From Lemma \ref{tr1}, we have
\[
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*, w-\Psi(w)\rangle
\ge
(1- \aleph) \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2 \] and \[(1- \aleph)\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|\leq\|w-\Psi(w)\|
\le
\mathcal (1+\aleph) \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|.
\]
Thus,
\begin{align}\label{THL2}
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
&\le
-
(1- \aleph) \phi_1(s)
\frac{\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2}
{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1-\lambda_1}}
-
(1- \aleph) \phi_2(s)
\frac{\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2}
{(1- \aleph)^{1-\lambda_2}\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1-\lambda_2}}
\\
&=
-
\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}
\phi_1(s)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_1}
-
(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2} \phi_2(s)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_2}.
\end{align}
Combining \eqref{THL1} and \eqref{THL2}, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{ThL3}
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
&\le
-
2^{\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2}}
\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}
\phi_1(s)
{\mathcal{L}}^{\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2}}
-
2^{\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2}}
(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2}
\phi_2(s)
{\mathcal{L}}^{\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2}}.
\end{align}
Let
\(
\vartheta_1=\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2},\quad
\vartheta_2=\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2},
\)
\(
m_1=
2^{\vartheta_1}
\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}},
\) and \(
m_2=
2^{\vartheta_2}(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2}.
\) Then inequality \eqref{ThL3}, becomes
\[
\dot{\mathcal{L}}
\le
-
m_1 \phi_1(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\vartheta_1}
-
m_2 \phi_2(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\vartheta_2}.
\]
Applying Lemma \ref{lem2} with define
\(
\mathcal{F}_1(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \phi_1(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa},
\
\mathcal{F}_2(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \phi_2(\varkappa)\,d{\varkappa}
\). This establishes the FxT convergence of trajectory $w(s)$ to ${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$
, with the settling-time bound given by \eqref{eq_T_bound_lemma}.

label: DTHL2
title: Proof
body_md:
Differentiating the function \eqref{THL1} along the model trajectories. Then by Assumption~\eqref{assINDIs} yields
\begin{equation}
    \begin{split}
        \dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
&=
\left\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*,\dot w\right\rangle
\\
&=
-
\left(
\phi_1(s)\frac{1}{\|w-\Psi(w)\|^{1-\lambda_1}}
+
\phi_2(s)\frac{1}{\|w-\Psi(w)\|^{1-\lambda_2}}
\right)
\cdot
\langle w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*, w-\Psi(w)\rangle
\\&+ \delta\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2.
    \end{split}
\end{equation}
Using Lemma \ref{tr1}, we get 
\begin{equation}\label{DTHL2}
    \begin{split}
        \dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
&\le
-
(1- \aleph) \phi_1(s)
\frac{\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2}
{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1-\lambda_1}}
-
(1- \aleph) \phi_2(s)
\frac{\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2}
{(1- \aleph)^{1-\lambda_2}\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1-\lambda_2}}\\
&\qquad+ \delta\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2.
\\
&=
-
\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}
\phi_1(s)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_1}
-
(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2} \phi_2(s)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_2}\\
&\qquad+ \delta\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2.
    \end{split}
\end{equation}
If we suppose
\(
\Xi := \{w \mid \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|\le 1\}.
\) Then it is form two cases.\\

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Case 1:} If $w\in \Xi$. Since $0<\lambda_1<1$ with $\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|\le1$, it concluded that
\[
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2 - \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_1} \le 0.
\]
Thus,
\begin{equation}\label{ineq13}
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
\le
- N_1 \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_1}
- N_2 \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_2},
\end{equation}
where
\(
N_1 =\frac{(1- \aleph) \phi_1(s)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}-\delta,
\) and \(
N_2=
(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2} \phi_2(s)-\delta.
\) \\

\noindent
\textbf{Case 2:} If $w \notin \Xi$. Since $\lambda_2>1$ with $\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|>1$, it concluded that
\[
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^2 - \|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_2} \le 0.
\]
Thus, inequality \eqref{ineq13} is valid for both cases. Consequently, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
\le
-
\left(\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}
\phi_1(s)-\delta\right)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_1}
-
\left((1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2}\phi_2(s)-\delta\right)
\|w-{\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*\|^{1+\lambda_2}.
\end{equation*}
Equivalently, in terms of L, we have
\[
\dot{\mathcal{L}}(s,w(s))
\le
- 2^{\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2}}
\mathcal{F}_1(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\frac{1+\lambda_1}{2}}
-
2^{\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2}}
\mathcal{F}_2(s) {\mathcal{L}}^{\frac{1+\lambda_2}{2}}.
\]
where $\mathcal{F}_1=\frac{(1- \aleph)}{\mathcal (1+\aleph)^{1-\lambda_1}}
\phi_1(s)-\delta$ and $\mathcal{F}_2=(1- \aleph)^{\lambda_2}\phi_2(s)-\delta$. Therefore, it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem2} that $w(s)$ converges to 
${\overline{\mathfrak{w}}}^*$ within  $\mathrm{FxT}$.
